I am an environment and climate economist, currently pursuing a DPhil in Geography and Environment at the [University of Oxford](https://www.ox.ac.uk/). Growing up in Nepal, I was conscious of a fundamental development challenge: improving living standards requires greater economic opportunities, employment, and income generation, while climate change is already creating new pressures on development and resilience. My research is motivated by how developing and emerging economies can navigate these objectives together. I was drawn to economics because of its potential as a policy tool — to understand these trade-offs and inform decisions capable of making a difference at scale.

My path has taken me from studying economics at [Ashoka University](https://www.ashoka.edu.in/), to applied economic and policy research in Nepal, an MSc in Environmental Economics and Climate Change at the [London School of Economics](https://www.lse.ac.uk/geography-and-environment/), and research on carbon removl policy at Oxford's [Smith School of Enterprise and the Environment](https://www.smithschool.ox.ac.uk/). At the [School of Geography and the Environment](https://www.geog.ox.ac.uk/), my doctoral research examines climate-compatible growth in lower- and middle-income countries.

I hope to work at the interface of **research and policy**: producing rigorous research while also translating and communicating evidence in ways that can inform public policy.

I am a co-convener of the Early Career Research Group at the [School of Geography and the Environment, University of Oxford](https://www.geog.ox.ac.uk/).

Outside academia, I enjoy writing and cooking. Alongside my DPhil, I am writing a memoir about the lives of my grandmothers. I hope to preserve their stories and perspectives, and through them record experiences of women's lives in Nepal that might otherwise go unrecorded.
